title: Around town: rickshaws, cabs & the metro
goal: Get a rickshaw and agree the fare, direct the driver turn by turn, book a cab, ride the metro and the bus, and ask how long it takes.
intro:
In unit 11 you learnt to ask the way. Now you're the one in the back of the rickshaw telling the driver where to go — and in Gujarat that means landmarks (**સર્કલ**, **ચાર રસ્તા**, **સિગ્નલ**, 'the petrol pump'), a bit of friendly haggling, and a lot of **ઊભી રાખો**, **ઉતારી દો**, **ડાબે લઈ લો**.

Those are **compound verbs**: a main verb plus a helper like **દેવું**, **લેવું** or **જવું**, and they're what makes Gujarati instructions sound natural. You'll also learn how to say how long a journey takes with **લાગવું**: **કેટલી વાર લાગશે?** 'how long will it take?'

grammar.title: Compound verbs: ઊભી રાખો, ઉતારી દો, બેસી જાઓ
grammar.body:
A **compound verb** is a main verb in its **-ઈ** form plus a helper verb that carries the tense and person. The helper loses its own meaning and adds a flavour:

**દેવું** 'give' → done outward, for someone else, completely: **ઉતારી દો** 'drop me off', **કહી દે** 'just tell (them)', **કૅન્સલ કરી દીધું** 'cancelled it'.
**લેવું** 'take' → done for yourself, towards you: **લઈ લો** 'take it', **ડાબે લઈ લો** 'take a left', **બુક કરી લીધી** 'booked it (for us)'.
**જવું** 'go' → a change of state or position, completed: **ઊતરી જાઓ** 'get off', **બેસી જાઓ** 'hop in', **પહોંચી ગયા** 'we're there'.

In requests compound verbs sound natural and decisive, not rude, and they combine with every politeness level: **ઉતારી દે** (friend), **ઉતારી દો** (driver), **ઉતારી દેજો** (later / softer), **ઉતારી દેશો?** (very polite).

**ઊભું રાખવું** 'to stop (a vehicle)' agrees with the vehicle: રિક્ષા **ઊભી** રાખો, સ્કૂટર **ઊભું** રાખો.

The trap: negatives normally use the **simple** verb, not the compound: **અહીં ના ઉતારશો** 'don't drop me here', not ~~ઉતારી ના દેશો~~.

grammar.title: How long it takes: લાગવું
grammar.body:
'It takes (time)' is **લાગવું** — the same verb as 'to seem' and 'to feel'. The **time is the subject**; the person, if mentioned, takes **-ને**:

**વીસ મિનિટ લાગે છે** 'it takes twenty minutes'
**મને અડધો કલાક લાગશે** 'it'll take me half an hour'
**કેટલી વાર લાગશે?** / **કેટલો ટાઇમ લાગશે?** 'how long will it take?'

In the past it **agrees with the time**: એક કલાક **લાગ્યો** (m), વીસ મિનિટ **લાગી** (f), બે કલાક **લાગ્યા** (pl).

**Doing what**: put the verb in the **-તાં** form: **ઑફિસ પહોંચતાં** 'in getting to the office', **ચાલતાં** 'on foot (walking)': **ચાલતાં દસ મિનિટ થાય** 'it's ten minutes' walk' (**થવું** works too for rough estimates).

**Distance** is **કેટલું દૂર?** or **કેટલું અંતર છે?** 'how far?'

The trap: don't use લેવું 'take' as in English: ~~વીસ મિનિટ લે છે~~ is wrong; time **લાગે છે**.

examples.en: How long will it take from here to the airport?
It takes twenty minutes by metro.

examples.en: There was traffic, so it took an hour.

culture: In Gujarat the auto-rickshaw is simply **રિક્ષા**, and its driver is **ભાઈ** (or **કાકા** if older); he'll call you **બેન** or **ભાઈ** / **સાહેબ**. Meters exist, but outside the big stations many drivers quote a price, so agree it **before** you get in — friendly, not angry, haggling is normal. Ahmedabad also has **શટલ રિક્ષા**, shared rickshaws that run fixed routes for a few rupees a seat. Directions are given by landmarks rather than street names: the **સર્કલ**, the **ચાર રસ્તા**, the petrol pump, a temple, a well-known sweet shop. Getting around Ahmedabad there's also the BRTS (**જનમાર્ગ**) and AMTS buses and, since 2022, the metro; between cities people take the **એસ.ટી.** (state transport) bus or a train, and on the S.G. Highway everyone seems to be on an Activa. Ride apps (Uber, Ola, Rapido bike taxis) are everywhere in the cities; the driver will phone to ask **ક્યાં છો?** and then **ઓટીપી બોલો**. Payment is increasingly by UPI — **ઑનલાઇન આપું?** — though it's still wise to carry small notes.

tip.title: Agree the fare first
tip.body:
- Ask with the polite future: **X આવશો?** 'will you go to X?' · **કેટલા લેશો?** 'how much?'
- Counter with your own future: **સો આપીશ** 'I'll give a hundred'.
- Call the driver **ભાઈ** or **કાકા**, keep it friendly, and agree the price before you get in.

lessons.title: Telling the driver where to go

tip.title: Compound verbs: ઉતારી દો, લઈ લો
tip.body:
- Main verb in **-ઈ** + a helper: **ઉતારી દો** 'drop me', **ડાબે લઈ લો** 'take a left', **ઊતરી જાઓ** 'get off'.
- **દેવું** = for someone else, **લેવું** = for yourself, **જવું** = a change completed.
- **ઊભું રાખવું** agrees with the vehicle: રિક્ષા **ઊભી** રાખો.
- Negatives use the simple verb: અહીં **ના ઉતારશો**.

tip.title: It takes: લાગવું
tip.body:
- Time 'is felt': **વીસ મિનિટ લાગે છે** 'it takes twenty minutes'; **કેટલી વાર લાગશે?**
- In the past it agrees with the time: એક કલાક **લાગ્યો** (m), વીસ મિનિટ **લાગી** (f).
- 'To do it': the **-તાં** form: **પહોંચતાં**, **ચાલતાં**.
- Not ~~લે છે~~ as in English 'takes'.

tip.title: English word + કરવું, often as a compound
tip.body:
- Apps are all English nouns + **કરવું**: કૅબ **બુક કરવી**, રાઇડ **કૅન્સલ કરવી**.
- Compounds make it sound done and dusted: **બુક કરી દઉં?** 'shall I book it?', **બુક કરી લીધી** 'I've booked it'.
- In the past the verb agrees with the object: કૅબ (f) → કરી **લીધી**.
tip.pattern: … બુક / કૅન્સલ + કરી દો / કરી લીધી

lessons.title: On the metro and the bus

tip.title: Getting on, off and changing
tip.body:
- **X-માં ચડવું** 'get on X' · **Y પર / Y-એ ઊતરવું** 'get off at Y' · **બદલવું** 'change'.
- Compounds again: **ચડી જા!** 'get on!', **ઊતરી જજો** 'get off (there)'.
- 'Where do I get off?' is just the infinitive: **ક્યાં ઊતરવું?**
- 'Have to change' agrees with the vehicle: મેટ્રો **બદલવી** પડશે (f).
tip.pattern: X-માં ચડો · Y પર ઊતરી જાઓ
